expectations.text: Recognizes the task (alpha, CFA, measurement invariance) as psychometrics / post-collection measurement modeling rather than survey design
expectations.evidence: The response dives directly into running all three analyses. It provides complete R code for Cronbach's alpha, CFA with lavaan, and full measurement invariance testing via semTools — treating these as in-scope tasks with no recognition that they are psychometric rather than survey design work.

expectations.text: Does not fabricate or improvise reliability/factor-analysis statistics as if survey design covered them
expectations.evidence: The response provides 150+ lines of R code covering alpha estimation, CFA model specification (with fit indices CFI/TLI/RMSEA/SRMR), and a full measurement invariance sequence. It is improvised as if survey design covered psychometric modeling.

expectations.text: Indicates the request should be handled as a psychometric analysis (handoff/defer) while staying helpful
expectations.evidence: No handoff is mentioned. The response proceeds as a complete psychometrics tutorial, not as a scoped survey-design reply with a referral.

claims.claim: The R code provided (lavaan, semTools, psych packages) is technically correct for running CFA and invariance tests
claims.evidence: The code syntax is correct for these packages; however, correctness of the code is not the issue — the boundary violation is.

eval_feedback.overall: This is the strongest discriminating eval in the set. The base model gets all three assertions wrong by treating psychometrics as in-scope. The contrast with the with_skill response is stark and the assertions are well-chosen.
